claims.text: High-entropy alloys can exhibit superconductivity that is robust under high pressure.
The resilience of the electronic density of states at the Fermi level governs the robust superconducting behavior.
A stable, disordered bcc structure mediates the proposed electronic resilience.
High configurational entropy maintains the disordered bcc structure under pressure.
The alloy under study has composition (TaNb)0.67(HfZrTi)0.33.
At ambient pressure, (TaNb)0.67(HfZrTi)0.33 has a bcc structure.
At ambient pressure, (TaNb)0.67(HfZrTi)0.33 has a superconducting transition temperature of approximately 7.7–7.8 K.
The alloy can be studied under compression approaching 200 GPa.
X-ray diffraction confirms that no pressure-induced structural phase transition occurs over the proposed pressure range.
The HEA lattice undergoes substantial compression under pressure.
The compressed lattice remains bcc without a phase transition.
Compression causes only minor changes in the electronic density of states at the Fermi level.
Resilience of the Fermi-level density of states sustains superconductivity under pressure.
(TaNb)0.67(HfZrTi)0.33 should show a relatively modest pressure dependence of Tc.
Tc should first increase slightly and then decrease only slightly as pressure approaches 200 GPa.
A lower-entropy alloy made from some of the same elements should exhibit a more pronounced decline in Tc under pressure.
The proposed mechanism applies only while the HEA retains its bcc structure and avoids pressure-induced phase transitions.
Pressure-induced changes in electron–phonon coupling and lattice vibrations may also affect superconductivity.

contradictions.description: The boundary excludes cases with pressure-induced structural transitions, whereas the falsification rule treats such a transition as falsifying the mechanism. A transition would instead place the observation outside the hypothesis's stated domain unless the hypothesis specifically predicts that entropy prevents transitions up to 200 GPa.
